commit.message:
Leave out of the sender's set the pull requests rule 0 finds with the agents (S-001 stage 1b)

The phone's sender now judges each pull request by J22's rule 0 through the
shared module the board uses (src/lib/j22.js), fed the same inputs: the
required reviewers from the checkout's governance/risk-paths.toml and J20's
list at the head; each verdict blob read once by its sha (git/blobs) and kept
in J18 by its keyed hash; a verdict file only on the default branch read from
the checkout; the owner check only where the page reads it (a public v3
project, the shared ownerChecksApply), for the heads ownerCheckHeads chooses,
conditional with J18's ETag, made last in the run and skipped below 400
remaining or with no header. Failed, refused, 404, oversized, non-text or
mismatched blobs count as given and are not kept; a failed owner check is
"not read". J18's new rule-0 part is sealed and counted toward the 5,000.

Tests: notify-j16-rule0 (17), notify-j18-rule0 (3), notify-ac73-rule0 (7),
real-on-real against the page's scheduler on #126, #128, #130, #135 and #148
with their real verdict blobs recorded under tests/desk/fixtures/j22/blobs/.

Test the sender's rule 0 read limits so each check is reached (S-001 stage 1b, review round 1)

B1: two verdict blobs whose sha is the real blob sha of their bytes, so they
pass the sha, length and form checks and reach the UTF-8 decode and the 1 MB
checks: "Verdict: FAIL\n" with 0xff 0xfe after it, and with 1 MiB of "a"
after it; each counted as given, not kept, and asked again next run. The
earlier cases stay, testing the sha, length and form checks.
N1: the rule-0 part's bad cases now use well-formed keys, so each reaches its
own check (the word, the ETag, the state, `after`, the entry's and the part's
fields), each asserted by its reason.
N2: the 1 MB and UTF-8 limits on a verdict read from the checkout, and the
client's remaining count reset by a network failure and by an uncredentialed
download.
